title: Practice midterm 1
description: 35 multiple choice + 15 blanks: World Bank (1993), Vogel, Fasteau & Fletcher (Japan, Korea), Tomeczek.

items.q: Which group correctly lists the eight "high-performing Asian economies" (HPAEs) in the World Bank (1993) report?
choices: Japan; Hong Kong, Korea, Singapore, Taiwan; Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand
Japan; Hong Kong, Korea, Singapore, Taiwan; China, the Philippines, Vietnam
Japan, China, Korea, Taiwan, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand
Hong Kong, Korea, Singapore, Taiwan, China, India, the Philippines, Thailand
items.explanation: Japan + the Four Tigers + three Southeast Asian NIEs. China is explicitly left out of the study.
notes: China is left out of the study (WB 1)
Made up. China and India aren't HPAEs

items.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the "Four Tigers"?
choices: Hong Kong
Singapore
Malaysia
Korea
items.explanation: Malaysia is one of the three Southeast Asian NIEs, with Indonesia and Thailand.

items.q: According to the World Bank (1993), roughly how much of the HPAEs' growth is accounted for by high investment and human capital (accumulation)?
choices: one-third
one-half
two-thirds
nine-tenths
items.explanation: Accumulation ≈ two-thirds; productivity growth = the rest.

items.q: Find a FALSE statement about the World Bank's (1993) account of the HPAEs.
choices: The HPAEs combined rapid growth with falling income inequality.
Investment averaged more than 20 percent of GDP in 1960–90.
Education spending went mainly to universities, not schools.
Inflation averaged about 9 percent, vs 18 percent elsewhere.
items.explanation: The opposite: spending went to primary and secondary schools; universities were left mostly to private funding.
notes: True: other low- and middle-income economies (WB 12)

items.q: The idea that East Asian governments deliberately "got the prices wrong" to boost industries is associated with which view?
choices: the neoclassical view
the revisionist view (Amsden 1989)
the market-friendly view (WDR 1991)
the dependency view
items.explanation: Revisionists: governments "led the market"
notes: Says governments mostly left prices to markets (WB 9)
The World Bank's own earlier view: government helps markets, doesn't replace them (WB 9)
Made up. Not one of the views in the reading

items.q: What does the World Bank (1993) mean by "deliberation councils"?
choices: secret meetings where firms lobby politicians for special favours
forums where private-sector groups help shape and carry out policy
courts that settle disputes between rival government ministries
labour unions that negotiate wages directly with the government
items.explanation: Unlike lobbying, the councils make allocation rules clear to everyone. Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Singapore.
notes: The opposite: councils made the rules open to everyone (WB 14)
Made up. Labour was largely left out

items.q: What does the World Bank call the practice of holding deposit and lending rates below market-clearing levels?
choices: financial liberalization
quantitative easing
financial repression
capital flight
items.explanation: Mild version = real rates positive but low. Transfers income from households (savers) to firms (borrowers)
notes: Made up. A modern central-bank term, not in the reading

items.q: Which of the following was NOT one of the mechanisms the World Bank lists as showing that "all would have a share of future wealth" (the principle of shared growth)?
choices: comprehensive land reform in Korea and Taiwan
rice and fertilizer price policies in Indonesia
massive public housing programs in Hong Kong and Singapore
nationalization of all private banks in Japan
items.explanation: The listed ones: land reform (Korea, Taiwan), rice and fertilizer prices (Indonesia), public housing (Hong Kong, Singapore), plus Malaysia's wealth-sharing for ethnic Malays.

items.q: According to the World Bank (1993), which Japanese ministry acted as a check on MITI's ability to carry out subsidy policies?
choices: the Ministry of Finance
the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
the Ministry of Construction
the Ministry of Agriculture
items.explanation: MOF checked MITI. In Indonesia and Thailand, balanced-budget laws did the same job

items.q: How did Chalmers Johnson (1982) famously describe Japan's postwar politics?
choices: Bureaucrats reigned while politicians ruled.
Politicians reigned while bureaucrats ruled.
Business reigned while politicians ruled.
The emperor reigned while the LDP ruled.
items.explanation: Politicians reigned, bureaucrats ruled (actually ran the country). Easy to swap

items.q: What did Muramatsu and Krauss (1987) call the Japanese political system?
choices: corporatism without labor
bureaupluralism
patterned pluralism
the developmental state
items.explanation: Vogel calls patterned pluralism "descriptively accurate yet analytically misleading".

items.q: How did Ramseyer and Rosenbluth (1993) turn Johnson's thesis on its head?
choices: They argued that business, not bureaucrats, really controlled policy.
They cast politicians as "principals" and bureaucrats as "agents."
They argued that the courts, not ministries, dominated policymaking.
They cast bureaucrats as "principals" and politicians as "agents."
items.explanation: Vogel's criticism: they ignored how bureaucrats manipulated politicians. Kato (1994) looked at both directions.
notes: Swapped. That's closer to Johnson's original view (V 101)

items.q: In the jankenpon (rock, paper, scissors) model described by Vogel, which pattern is correct?
choices: Politicians beat bureaucrats, bureaucrats beat industry, industry beats politicians.
Bureaucrats beat politicians, politicians beat industry, industry beats bureaucrats.
Industry beats bureaucrats, bureaucrats beat politicians, politicians beat industry.
Politicians beat both industry and bureaucrats, and neither beats politicians.
items.explanation: From Iio (2008). So bureaucrats got industry to lobby politicians for them.
notes: Made up. It's a cycle, so nobody wins outright

items.q: Which is NOT one of the three distinctive features of Japan's postwar model according to Vogel (2021)?
choices: Officials held their own policy preferences, apart from societal interests.
Officials actively manipulated politicians to reach their goals.
Officials played a political role balancing interests in their sector.
Officials simply carried out positions written for them by Keidanren.
items.explanation: The Keidanren story shows the reverse: MPT officials told Keidanren what to ask for.

items.q: In Vogel's account of the "Telecom Wars" of the 1980s, which ministries fought, and who won?
choices: MITI and MOF; MOF won
MPT and MITI; MPT won
MPT and MITI; MITI won
MOF and MPT; MOF won
items.explanation: MPT (communications) vs MITI (computers) over the emerging IT sector. MPT won. The MPT official needed a second subway pass to Keidanren

items.q: What are shingikai?
choices: LDP factions inside the Diet
policy councils run by the ministries
post-retirement jobs for bureaucrats
presidents' clubs of keiretsu firms
items.explanation: Ministry officials controlled membership and agenda. MITI councils = manufacturing, MOF councils = finance

items.q: According to Vogel, when did the Japanese bureaucracy enjoy its "heyday of power"?
choices: the Meiji era only
the 1950s to the early 1970s
the bubble years of the late 1980s
after the 2001 administrative reform
items.explanation: Decline from the 1970s (slower growth, MOF budget ceilings contested, the rise of zoku), then the 1990s crash and scandals.
notes: Made up. Decline had already started (V 107)

items.q: Find a TRUE statement about the 1994 political reform.
choices: It replaced a two-party system with a multiparty system.
It mixed 300 single-member seats with 200 PR seats, ending SNTV.
It was passed by the LDP government of Prime Minister Hashimoto.
It created 511 single-member districts across the country.
items.explanation: Passed by the Hosokawa coalition in January 1994. The old system had 130 multi-member districts and 511 seats.
notes: Made up. The aim was closer to the reverse (V 107)
Passed by the Hosokawa coalition; Hashimoto did the 2001 reform (V 107–108)
511 was the old total of seats (V 107)

items.q: The administrative reorganization launched by Prime Minister Hashimoto and implemented in January 2001 reduced the number of cabinet-level ministries and agencies from ___ to ___.
items.explanation: Also created the Cabinet Office and the CEFP (which took budgeting power from MOF)

items.q: Which body, created under the second Abe administration in 2014, gave the prime minister and cabinet greater control over the appointments of top bureaucrats?
choices: the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy
the Cabinet Bureau of Personnel Affairs
the Economic Planning Agency
the Policy Affairs Research Council
items.explanation: Naikaku jinjikyoku (2014). The DPJ had failed three times to pass it.
notes: Created in 2001, took budgeting power from MOF (V 108)
Made up. Abolished in the 2001 reform
The LDP's own policy body, not a cabinet office

items.q: In Vogel's discussion of the Moritomo Gakuen scandal, what does sontaku mean?
choices: bribery of a minister
preemptive action to satisfy superiors
a formal order from the prime minister
the leaking of documents to the press
items.explanation: MOF officials deleted references to Akie Abe in the land-sale documents
notes: Made up. The point is nobody gave an order

items.q: According to Fasteau and Fletcher (2024), what are the two kinds of industrial policy Japan has employed?
choices: import-substitution policy and export-promotion policy
catch-up policy (CUIP, to 1990) and mature-economy policy (MEIP)
military industrial policy and civilian industrial policy
neoclassical industrial policy and revisionist industrial policy
items.explanation: CUIP from roughly 1870 to 1990; MEIP since then.
notes: Made up. Development-economics terms, not FF's
Those are views of the HPAEs in the World Bank reading (WB 9)

items.q: Find a FALSE statement about the Fiscal Investment and Loan Program (FILP).
choices: It let MOF lend postal savings and pension funds to strategic industries.
It ranged from 3.3 percent of GDP in 1956 to 6.3 percent in 1972.
For decades, MITI and MOF officials set it with little political input.
It was controlled directly by the LDP's Policy Affairs Research Council.
items.explanation: It was made by bureaucrats, with little political input

items.q: What role did the Development Bank of Japan (DBJ) play, according to Fasteau and Fletcher?
choices: It financed most of Japan's industrial investment by itself.
Its small loans signalled to banks which industries to back.
It set and controlled the yen's exchange rate with MOF.
It regulated the stock market and supervised listed firms.
items.explanation: A signalling role: the government was implicitly guaranteeing those industries. FILP money was usually channelled through the DBJ.
notes: Made up. The yen was fixed at 360 under Bretton Woods (FF-J 103)

items.q: According to Fasteau and Fletcher, policy in Japan was set by the "iron triangle" of ______.
choices: the emperor, the military, and the LDP
big business, the bureaucracy, and the LDP
labour unions, farmers, and the JSP
the US, MITI, and MOF
items.explanation: Collective leadership, not strong individual leaders

items.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the six major postwar horizontal keiretsu named by Fasteau and Fletcher?
choices: Sumitomo
Fuyo
Sanwa
Toyota
items.explanation: The six: Sumitomo, Mitsui, Mitsubishi, Fuyo, Daiichi Kangyo, Sanwa. Each was centred on a bank; the first four have prewar zaibatsu roots. Toyota heads a supply-chain keiretsu

items.q: Which of the following do Fasteau and Fletcher call one of MITI's "more notorious mistakes"?
choices: supporting the steel industry
trying to keep Honda making only motorcycles
promoting the semiconductor industry
joining the OECD and GATT too early
items.explanation: Firms also overruled MITI's plans to consolidate the auto and computer industries.
notes: Made up. Steel was a success story

items.q: At what rate was the yen fixed against the US dollar from 1949 to 1971?
choices: 100 yen
240 yen
308 yen
360 yen
items.explanation: Under Bretton Woods. Nixon ended the peg in 1971
notes: The Smithsonian rate after 1971 (not in the reading)

items.q: According to Tomeczek (2022), the 1947 Anti-Monopoly Law made holding companies illegal. In what year were holding companies legalized again?
items.explanation: Part of the 1990s deregulation

items.q: Find a FALSE statement about keiretsu institutions (Tomeczek 2022).
choices: The shachō-kai is the presidents' club of a horizontal keiretsu.
The kyōryoku-kai is the suppliers' association of a vertical keiretsu.
The sōgō shōsha is the general trading company of the keiretsu.
The shachō-kai exists in both horizontal and vertical keiretsu.
items.explanation: Shachō-kai exist only in horizontal keiretsu; the vertical equivalent is the kyōryoku-kai

items.q: After a series of mergers of keiretsu main banks, which three "super-keiretsu" financial groups remain today?
choices: Mitsubishi UFJ, Sumitomo Mitsui, and Mizuho
Nomura, Daiwa, and Nikko
Mitsubishi UFJ, Nomura, and Japan Post
Mitsui, Mitsubishi, and Yasuda
items.explanation: Three bank groups formed from mergers of the old keiretsu main banks.
notes: Mixed list: Nomura is a securities firm

items.q: After taking power in a coup in May 1961, Park Chung Hee created a new "superministry" with wide-ranging powers to coordinate other ministries. What was it?
choices: the Ministry of Reconstruction
the Economic Planning Board (EPB)
the Korea Development Bank
the Fair Trade Commission
items.explanation: The EPB was abolished in 1994.
notes: A state bank, not a superministry

items.q: Which of the following was NOT a chaebol?
choices: Samsung
Hyundai
Daewoo
POSCO
items.explanation: POSCO (Pohang Iron and Steel) was a state-owned enterprise, not part of any group. The 1975 chaebol list: Samsung, Lucky (LG), Hyundai, Hanjin, Hyosung, SsangYong, Daewoo.

items.q: Find a TRUE statement about POSCO, according to Fasteau and Fletcher.
choices: The World Bank strongly recommended building it in the 1960s.
Japanese "reparations" helped fund it after the World Bank said no.
It was created by the Samsung group as its first steel company.
Its first plant opened two years behind the original schedule.
items.explanation: Japan's 1968–9 payments helped fund it. Run by Park Tae-Joon, a retired general.
notes: Backwards. A World Bank study said it wasn't feasible (FF-K 10)
Backwards. Two months ahead of schedule, 1973 (FF-K 10)

items.q: As a condition of the IMF package approved on December 3, 1997, what cap was imposed on chaebol borrowing?
choices: debt limited to 100 percent of equity
debt limited to 200 percent of equity
debt limited to 400 percent of equity
no cap on borrowing was imposed
items.explanation: The package was $58 billion. Debt-to-equity had reached almost 400% by 1997.
notes: Roughly where debt-to-equity already was by 1997 (FF-K 8)
